verdict.rationale: Hyperbrowser's open-source HyperAgent extends Playwright with AI, letting you 'write natural language commands instead of complex selectors'. The evidence shows this via page.ai("search for flights... select the cheapest option"), which drives the page through described intents rather than selectors. However, page.ai is shown as a task-level command, not as granular act/click/type primitives on single described elements. Resilience to selector and layout changes is only implied by avoiding selectors. Missing for 10: documented element-level act/click/type primitives, an explicit claim or test of robustness to DOM/layout changes, and independent or hands-on corroboration.
